recap.back_html: At each position, the patch times the kernel, element by element, summed. The outputs form a feature map.
out * in * k * k weights plus out biases. Independent of image size.
No. It computes cross-correlation, the plain sliding sum.

snippets: def correlate(image, kernel):
kh, kw = kernel.shape
out = np.zeros((image.shape[0] - kh + 1, image.shape[1] - kw + 1))
for i in range(out.shape[0]):
for j in range(out.shape[1]):
out[i, j] = (image[i:i + kh, j:j + kw] * kernel).sum()
return out
lessons.takeaway_html: A convolution slides one small set of shared weights across the image. It is local, it works the same everywhere, and training learns its weights.
lessons.title: Convolution, a small filter slid across an image

recap.back_html: (H + 2 * padding - kernel_size) // stride + 1, for height and width alike.
Stride 1 and padding (k - 1) / 2, or padding='same' (stride 1 only).
recap.front_html: Keep the size with a k by k kernel

recap.back_html: (N, C, H, W). Convert (N, H, W, C) with x.permute(0, 3, 1, 2), never reshape.
(out_channels, in_channels, kH, kW).

lessons.takeaway_html: Conv2d reads (N, C, H, W). Output size is (H + 2p - k) // s + 1. Pad to keep the size, stride to shrink it, and permute images that arrive channels last.
lessons.title: Padding, stride, channels and the (N, C, H, W) layout

recap.back_html: Largest value per non-overlapping 2 by 2 block. Halves height and width, rounding down. No weights.
channels * H * W of the last feature map. Work it out with the size rule, layer by layer.
End the convolutions with nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1), then Flatten and Linear(channels, classes).

recap.back_html: Conv2d (padding to keep the size), ReLU, MaxPool2d(2). Each block halves the map and grows the channels.
